title: ExxonMobil (XOM) Price Forecast: Pullback Tests Breakout Structure - FXEmpire
content: The stock of Exxon Mobile Corporation (XOM) recently confirmed bullish price action with a breakout above a double bottom pattern and the 50-day moving average. The initial move was followed by a reversal, forming a lower swing high at $163.68 and a bearish reversal on Wednesday. ExxonMobil is a leading global integrated oil and gas company and sellers remained in control of the company’s stock on Thursday. XOM broke back below the 50-day average to reach a low of $153.46 and the 50% retracement of the prior advance. Also, that was almost a test of support near the 20-day moving average near $152.73. Nonetheless, the 20-day average marks the next key support zone, followed by the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement at $151.47. This sequence reflects a typical post-breakout retest phase, where early gains are being evaluated by the market. XOM is in its first pullback following a significant breakout and bullish reversal signal that suggests that the bearish correction is complete, and the larger advance can continue. However, further evidence is needed. Specifically, a renewed recovery above the neckline of the double bottom at $155.69 and the 50-day average, now around $155.61, would be required to reassert bullish control. A declining trend channel is also included on the chart, suggesting that it could indicate further downside pressure. But first support above the 61.8% retracement would need to fail to confirm a deeper downside continuation. Otherwise, the expectation is for the pullback to find support and eventually resolve to the upside as buyers get more aggressive. A continuation of the developing uptrend based on structure will not confirm until there is a recovery of this week’s lower swing high at $163.68, which now serves as a key near-term pivot following the initial breakout attempt described above. The weekly chart confirms strong support near recent lows as represented by the rising 20-week moving average. It is now near $149.24 and marks another potentially significant support zone. On the daily chart, the 100-day moving average is in a similar position and is around $147.76 currently. It represents the low end of dynamic trend support. Since it was tested recently with the second bottom and higher swing low of $143.92, it is anticipated to do so again. Taken together, these higher-timeframe support levels help frame the current pullback as a test of the prior breakout structure, reinforcing that the broader trend initiate by the double bottom remains technically intact unless these support areas begin to fail. title: Can ConocoPhillips Sustain Long-Term Growth in the Lower 48? - The Globe and Mail
content: ConocoPhillips COP maintains a strong presence in the Lower 48 region through its resource-rich portfolio in the prolific Permian Basin. This region offers low production costs and rapid extraction cycles. The company significantly expanded its footprint after acquiring Marathon Oil Corporation. Building on this expanded footprint, COP continues to leverage its operational expertise to maximize scale and efficiency across the Lower 48 operations. Since 2023, the majority of ConocoPhillips’ exploration success has come from unconventional plays in the Permian Basin within the Lower 48. In the first quarter of 2026, COP produced 1.453 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (MMboe/d) from its Lower 48 region, representing nearly 63% of its total production. To increase Lower 48 production, the company drilled longer horizontal wells in the first quarter of 2026 compared with the prior-year period. This approach allows the upstream player to extract more oil and gas per well while reducing costs and boosting efficiency. During the first quarter of 2026, the company invested $2.9 billion in its operations, primarily focusing on short-cycle Lower 48 projects that can deliver quicker production and cash flow. ConocoPhillips increased its capital expenditure guidance for 2026 and projected a capital budget in the range of $12-$12.5 billion to fund development drilling, major projects and activities designed to generate long-term growth. These strategic investments and operational advancements ensure the company remains positioned for sustained long-term production growth. Energy players like ExxonMobil CorporationXOM and Chevron CorporationCVX maintain a strong presence in the Permian Basin, one of the most prolific basins in the United States. ExxonMobil holds a footprint of approximately 1.4 million net acres across the Permian Basin's Delaware and Midland sub-basins. By utilizing advanced techniques like cube development and proprietary proppant solutions, the company enhances operational efficiency and scale. These initiatives are designed to boost capital efficiency and help XOM achieve its target of roughly 2.5 MMboe/d in Permian output by 2030. Chevron also maintains a significant presence in the Permian Basin. CVX reported first-quarter 2026 production of 3.86 million barrels per day, up 15% year over year. This increase was driven by the Hess merger and higher output from the Permian Basin and the Gulf of Mexico. ConocoPhillips shares have gained 42% over the past year compared with 36.4% growth of the industry. From a valuation standpoint, COP trades at a trailing 12-month enterprise-value-to-EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) of 6.68X. This is above the broader industry average of 5.61X. With fears dominating the market, it is ideal for investors to increase their allocation to low-beta stocks. Stocks that may attract investors' attention are Liquidia Corp., Exxon Mobil Corp., Valero Energy Corp. and Diamondback Energy, Inc.. Beta measures the volatility or risk of a particular asset compared to the market. In other words, beta measures the extent of a security's price movement relative to the market. In this article, we are considering the S&P 500 as the market. If a stock has a beta of 1, then the price of the stock will move with the market. So, the stock is more volatile than the market if its beta is more than 1. In the same way, the stock is not as volatile as the market if its beta is less than 1. For example, if the market offers a return of 20%, a stock with a beta of 3 will return 60%, which is overwhelming. Similarly, when the market slips 20%, the stock will sink 60%, which is devastating. Here are four of the 39 stocks that qualified for the screening: Liquidia is experiencing rapid growth in YUTREPIA adoption, with increasing patient referrals, expanding prescriber base and rising market share. title: Is Exxon Mobil's Recent Surge Sustainable Amid Middle East Tensions - Kavout
content: Exxon Mobil (XOM) stock has been a standout performer in recent weeks, with shares trading at $154.19 as of March 2, 2026, up 1.11% on the day and nearing its 52-week high of $159.35. This impressive run, which saw the stock climb from $115.15 on November 30, 2025, to $152.50 by March 1, 2026—a 32.4% increase—is largely attributed to a dramatic shift in the global energy landscape. The "Midnight Hammer" crisis in the Middle East, characterized by retaliatory strikes and a de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz, has injected a significant risk premium into crude oil markets. This geopolitical shock has sent oil prices soaring, with WTI crude currently at $71.15 per barrel, having recently spiked towards $73 and Brent crude briefly touching $100 per barrel. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for 20% of global seaborne oil, has seen shipping halted and war risk coverage cancelled by marine insurers, effectively stranding an estimated 15 million barrels per day (bpd) of global supply. This immediate supply disruption, combined with a perceived failure of OPEC+ to adequately increase production, has fueled a rapid "risk-off" rotation into hard assets like oil. The market's reaction on March 2, 2026, saw XOM and Occidental Petroleum (OXY) both climb 2.1% by midday, even as the broader S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite tumbled. This divergence underscores a fundamental reassessment of value in an uncertain geopolitical climate, where the "old economy" energy trade has become a defensive hedge. While the immediate catalyst is conflict, the underlying "AI Power Crunch"—the insatiable demand for energy to fuel massive data centers—is also contributing to a structural revaluation of energy companies. However, the sustainability of this surge hinges precariously on the resolution of the Strait of Hormuz standoff. Analysts warn that a diplomatic "off-ramp" within the next 72 hours could lead to a significant cooling of oil prices. Conversely, if the blockade persists, a "super-spike" toward $120 per barrel is possible, which would almost certainly tip the broader global economy into a recession by Q3 2026. This delicate balance means XOM's recent gains, while substantial, are tied to highly unpredictable global events. The current surge in oil prices provides a significant tailwind for Exxon Mobil's Q1 2026 earnings, potentially rewriting near-term cash flow math. Higher crude prices directly enhance the profitability of Exxon's Upstream segment, which saw a 41% increase in revenue in Q1 2025, including a remarkable 234% jump in its U.S. Upstream operations. This segment is particularly sensitive to commodity price fluctuations, making the current environment highly favorable for top-line growth and margin expansion. Despite a 6% decline in net profit and a 15% fall in EPS in Q1 2025 due to weaker refining margins and petrochemicals, the company demonstrated resilience later in the year. Exxon Mobil reported strong Q3 2025 earnings of $7.5 billion and $14.8 billion in cash flow, followed by a Q4 2025 EPS of $1.71, beating estimates. This consistent outperformance, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of earnings beats, suggests an underlying operational strength that can capitalize on improved market conditions. Analysts are already adjusting their expectations, with Bank of America raising ExxonMobil's price target from $135 to $151, reflecting confidence in enhanced future profitability due to the oil risk premium. The consensus Q1 2026 EPS is projected at approximately $1.53, a figure that could prove conservative if oil prices remain elevated throughout the quarter. Exxon's ability to generate substantial free cash flow, projected at $52 billion for the 2025-2026 period, further strengthens its financial position to navigate market dynamics. However, it's not a clear-cut picture. While Upstream benefits, the Energy Products (refining) and Chemical Products segments can face margin pressures. In Q1 2025, Energy Products revenue declined 4% and Chemical Products revenue fell 8%, largely due to falling refining margins and an oversupply in the global chemical market. Therefore, while high crude prices boost one side of the business, investors must monitor product solutions segment margins and overall production guidance during the Q1 2026 earnings call, expected in late April, to gauge the full impact. Beyond the immediate tailwinds from geopolitical tensions, Exxon Mobil's long-term investment thesis is underpinned by its strategic focus on "advantaged barrels" and robust production growth from key assets. The company's operations in Guyana, particularly the Stabroek block, are a cornerstone of this strategy. Projects like Uaru, expected to start up by year-end 2026 with a capacity of 250,000 b/d, and Whiptail, forecast to add another 250,000 b/d next year, are set to boost Guyana's daily oil production well beyond 1 million b/d. Exxon Mobil is also actively developing Guyana's significant recoverable gas resources, especially in the southeast part of the Stabroek block. The Hammerhead project, for instance, is designed to transport gas by pipeline to shore, complementing oil production. The company has already completed its first gas-to-energy pipeline, awaiting an onshore power plant to lower electricity costs in Guyana. This integrated approach to resource development highlights Exxon's commitment to maximizing value from its world-class geology and competitive development costs. The Permian Basin in the U.S. shale patch remains another critical growth engine. CEO Darren Woods has stated there is "no near-term peak Permian" for Exxon, citing over 40 technologies currently in testing to enhance recovery and efficiency. This focus on low-cost, high-margin production in both Guyana and the Permian has made XOM a "HALO" stock (Heavy-Asset, Low Obsolescence) for investors seeking stability and long-term value. Furthermore, Exxon Mobil's commitment to shareholder returns is a significant draw. The company has a strong track record of distributing capital through dividends and share repurchases, having distributed $9.4 billion in Q3 2025 and $9.5 billion in Q4 2025. As a dividend Aristocrat, boasting 26 consecutive annual dividend increases, XOM offers a compelling proposition for income-focused investors, signaling management's confidence in its ability to generate sustained free cash flow and maintain financial discipline. While Exxon Mobil benefits from current market dynamics, several significant risks could derail its long-term investment thesis. The most immediate concern remains commodity price volatility. Despite recent spikes, energy prices are inherently sensitive to geopolitical events, OPEC+ decisions, and global demand fluctuations. A sharp decline in prices, whether due to de-escalation in the Middle East, falling global demand, or oversupply, could significantly reduce ExxonMobil’s income, particularly in its highly profitable Upstream segment. Beyond oil prices, the company faces regulatory and political risks. Stricter environmental legislation globally, including potential bans on exploration in sensitive regions, new emissions standards, and tighter regulation of refining, could increase operating costs or limit production capacity. The accelerating global energy transition to lower-carbon sources poses a fundamental threat to long-term demand for fossil fuels, potentially diminishing Exxon Mobil's core product revenue streams and creating significant market risks. Exxon Mobil's diversified earnings are also susceptible to global chemical market oversupply and weak refining margins. As seen in Q1 2025, the chemical segment experienced substantial earnings reductions due to "bottom-of-cycle" margins. This cyclicality can act as a significant drag, even when other segments perform well. The capital-intensive nature of its upstream and downstream mix constrains revenue growth assumptions, keeping them modest at around 2.3%. Finally, valuation concerns persist among some analysts. With a TTM P/E ratio of 23.15 and a current price of $154.19, some models suggest the stock is trading at a premium. Analyst consensus price targets range around $140-$142, implying a modest downside from current levels. For instance, one model projects a $140.92 fair value, representing a 6% downside. While the company's beta of 0.35 reflects lower volatility than the broader market, a retreat in oil prices after tensions ease could expose valuation risks, making the stock less attractive at current levels. Navigating the current volatile energy market with Exxon Mobil requires a nuanced approach, balancing short-term tactical plays with long-term strategic considerations. For investors looking to capitalize on immediate geopolitical shocks, XOM's strong correlation with oil prices, coupled with its robust production and cash flow, makes it a compelling option. The stock's beta of 0.35 indicates lower volatility compared to the broader market, offering a degree of stability even in turbulent times. However, a purely short-term strategy is fraught with risk. The unpredictable nature of geopolitical events means any sudden de-escalation could lead to a sharp correction in oil prices and, consequently, in XOM's stock. Investors should consider XOM as a "HALO" stock, benefiting from heavy assets and low obsolescence, but remain vigilant. Monitoring key events like OPEC+ ministerial meetings for changes in production quotas, and geopolitical developments in critical regions like Guyana, is paramount. For long-term investors, Exxon Mobil's status as a dividend Aristocrat, with a current dividend yield of 2.6% and 26 consecutive annual increases, offers a compelling income component. This consistent return to shareholders, alongside disciplined capital allocation and share repurchase programs, provides a defensive moat against market fluctuations. The company's strategic investments in low-cost, high-return assets like the Permian and Guyana further solidify its long-term growth potential, irrespective of short-term price swings. To mitigate risks, diversification remains key. While XOM offers exposure to the energy sector, considering alternatives like ConocoPhillips (COP) for a more pure-play upstream focus, or Canadian Natural Resources (CNQ) for its strong inventory and capital discipline, could balance a portfolio. Ultimately, investors should maintain a conservative position sizing, perhaps 1% to 3% of their portfolio, given the stock's near-term volatility and the cyclical headwinds in its downstream and chemical segments. Exxon Mobil stands at a pivotal juncture, poised to benefit from current geopolitical tailwinds while navigating inherent industry volatility. Its strategic asset base and commitment to shareholder returns offer a compelling long-term narrative, but investors must remain acutely aware of the risks. title: Market Analysis-May 20th, 2026 - The Globe and Mail
content: Global stock markets continue to exhibit increasingly complex late-cycle dynamics, although today’s trading session reflected renewed investor optimism driven primarily by artificial intelligence-related earnings momentum, broad technology sector strength, and improving global risk appetite. American and Canadian markets finished broadly higher as large-cap technology stocks led gains in the lead up to Nvidia’s earnings release. The  Nvidia Corporation posted stronger-than-expected quarterly results, reporting fiscal quarterly revenue of approximately $81.6 billion, representing roughly 85% year-over-year growth, while adjusted EPS also exceeded consensus expectations as hyperscaler and enterprise AI spending continued to fuel exceptional demand for accelerated computing infrastructure and AI data center deployment. The company’s forward revenue guidance near $91 billion further reinforced investor expectations that the global AI infrastructure cycle remains in an aggressive expansion phase despite concerns surrounding China export restrictions, valuation compression risk, and increasing competitive pressures from custom AI semiconductor providers. The continued concentration of market leadership within mega-cap AI and semiconductor equities suggests that liquidity and momentum remain heavily skewed toward a narrow group of technology beneficiaries, although today’s rally also broadened into cyclicals, commodities, and crypto-related assets. Cryptocurrencies moved materially higher alongside stocks, while gold and silver prices also advanced, reflecting a market environment where risk  and inflation-hedging behavior are simultaneously strengthening. Oil prices are currently trading near $100 per barrel, further reinforcing the possibility that inflationary pressures may remain structurally elevated globally, particularly as geopolitical tensions and supply concerns continue to support energy markets. Persistently elevated crude prices increase the probability that central banks may maintain restrictive monetary policy for longer than previously anticipated, potentially creating renewed pressure on interest-rate-sensitive sectors later in the cycle. European markets also traded higher, supported by strength in technology and defense shares, while macro sentiment improved following a decline in UK inflation to approximately 2.8% driven largely by lower household energy costs. The moderation in UK inflation provided some temporary relief to investors hoping that disinflationary trends may gradually re-emerge across developed economies despite continued commodity price pressures elsewhere. Global fund managers reported increased equity allocations at a record pace during May, signaling a meaningful resurgence in institutional risk positioning and growing investor confidence that earnings growth, particularly AI-related growth can continue to offset concerns regarding valuations, inflation, and slowing economic momentum. Despite today’s bullish price action, underlying macro conditions still increasingly resemble a high-risk late-cycle environment characterized by elevated equity valuations, narrowing market leadership, persistent inflation risk, geopolitical instability, and historically stretched technical conditions within major technology and semiconductor indices. While strong corporate earnings and aggressive capital return programs continue to support investor sentiment in the near term, the combination of elevated oil prices, speculative positioning in AI-linked assets, and increasingly crowded institutional equity exposure suggests that downside volatility risk remains elevated if macroeconomic conditions deteriorate, inflation accelerates further, or earnings expectations begin to normalize. The broader market backdrop therefore continues to reflect a fragile equilibrium between powerful AI-driven growth optimism and rising systemic macroeconomic risks across global financial markets. title: Major Investor Lifts ExxonMobil (NYSE: XOM) Stake 920% as Broad Institutional Buying and a $1.03 Dividend Back Energy Giant - foreignpolicyjournal.com
content: By Ewan Scott | May 20, 2026 | Economy & Business, Featured, News & Analysis Little House Capital LLC expanded its position in ExxonMobil Corporation (NYSE: XOM) by 920.8% during the fourth quarter, acquiring an additional 38,010 shares to bring its total holding to 42,138 shares valued at approximately $5.07 million, according to the firm’s most recent 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The near tenfold increase makes ExxonMobil the 26th largest holding in Little House Capital’s portfolio, representing approximately 1.3% of the firm’s total investments, and reflects a decisive conviction trade in one of the most widely held energy names among institutional investors. Little House Capital was far from alone in building its XOM position during the period, with a range of other institutional managers also increasing their exposure. Maryland State Retirement and Pension System lifted its position by 2.6% in the third quarter, ending with 215,892 shares valued at $24.3 million, while Capital Investment Advisors LLC grew its stake by 6.6% in Q4 to 231,488 shares worth $27.9 million. New Age Alpha Advisors LLC increased its holding by 5.6% in Q3 to 166,547 shares, HORAN Wealth LLC lifted its position by 78.3% over the same period to 13,180 shares, and Krilogy Financial LLC raised its stake by 46.6% to 35,160 shares. Institutional investors now collectively own 61.80% of ExxonMobil’s outstanding stock, reflecting the company’s deep integration into pension, endowment, and wealth management portfolios globally. On the analyst side, Wall Street’s view on XOM is broadly constructive, with the stock carrying a consensus Moderate Buy rating derived from one Strong Buy, ten Buy, and ten Hold ratings, producing an average price target of $163.95. JPMorgan Chase raised its price target from $140 to $170 and maintained an Overweight designation, while Scotiabank lifted its target from $128 to $163 with a Sector Outperform rating, and TD Cowen trimmed its target modestly from $175 to $172 while maintaining a Buy. Mizuho raised its target from $140 to $162 but held a Neutral rating, and Loop Capital was the most cautious voice with a $123 target, reflecting the range of views on how much of the Iran conflict’s oil price tailwind is sustainable versus priced in. ExxonMobil opened at $162.71 on Wednesday May 20, within a 52-week range of $101.18 to $176.41 and above both its 50-day moving average of $155.46 and its 200-day moving average of $138.25, giving the stock a positive near-term technical setup. The company reported Q1 2026 earnings per share of $1.16, beating the consensus estimate of $0.98 by $0.18, on revenue of $83.16 billion against expectations of $81.13 billion, with revenue up 2.4% year-on-year and net margin of 7.57%. ExxonMobil declared a quarterly dividend of $1.03 per share payable on 10 June 2026, representing an annualised payout of $4.12 and a dividend yield of approximately 2.5%, with the payout ratio at 69.48%. A Texas jury recently cleared ExxonMobil of investor fraud claims, removing a headline legal risk that had been hanging over the stock, and the company has been cited in positive commentary comparing it to peer Chevron (NYSE: CVX) as a buy for income and value-oriented investors looking for exposure to an oil price environment that has been materially elevated by Middle East supply disruptions. Insider activity has been on the selling side, with Vice President Darrin L. Talley selling 2,150 shares on 2 March at an average price of $157.82 for proceeds of $339,313, leaving him with 18,204 shares, with company insiders collectively owning 0.03% of the total share count. The oil market backdrop, with Brent crude above $109 and WTI above $105 driven by the ongoing Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz concerns, provides a direct tailwind to ExxonMobil’s upstream earnings and underpins the bullish analyst positioning that has driven multiple price target increases over the past two months. Ewan is a reporter at the Foreign Policy Journal, primarily covering US current affairs and news related to NYSE-listed stocks. He has over two decades of experience in journalism and digital publishing.

In this article, we are considering the S&P 500 as the market. If a stock has a beta of 1, then the price of the stock will move with the market. So, the stock is more volatile than the market if its beta is more than 1. In the same way, the stock is not as volatile as the market if its beta is less than 1. For example, if the market offers a return of 20%, a stock with a beta of 3 will return 60%, which is overwhelming. title: ExxonMobil vs. Chevron: Better Energy Stock to Buy Now? - The Globe and Mail
content: ExxonMobil and Chevron are two of the largest oil companies in the world. While they're both similarly strong companies, one stands out as the best in the sector. ExxonMobil(NYSE: XOM) and Chevron(NYSE: CVX) are leaders in the oil patch. They both have globally integrated operations, low costs, fortress balance sheets, and excellent records of delivering value to shareholders. The energy giants also boast strong long-term growth outlooks. Given their similarly strong profiles, it can be difficult to decide which of these top energy stocks to buy. Here's a look at which one is the better buy right now. Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? Our team just released a report on the one little-known company, called an "Indispensable Monopoly" providing the critical technology Nvidia and Intel both need. Continue » ExxonMobil and Chevron share many similarities. However, when comparing these two large international oil companies (IOCs), it's abundantly clear that Exxon reigns supreme. Last year, the oil giant generated $28.8 billion in earnings and $52 billion in cash flow from operations, putting it well ahead of Chevron ($13.5 billion of earnings and $33.9 billion in cash flow from operations). Exxon not only bested its closest peer last year but has also delivered IOC-leading earnings and cash flow growth over the last five years (compound annual growth rates of more than 20% and 10%, respectively). Those aren't the only categories where Exxon leads all IOCs. As of the end of last year, Exxon had delivered $15.1 billion in cumulative structural cost savings since 2019, more than all other IOCs combined. It has also delivered an average return on capital employed of 11% since 2019, leading all IOC. Meanwhile, Exxon ended last year with an industry-leading balance sheet, backed by an ultra-low 11% net debt-to-capital ratio. Exxon's financial strength enabled it to pay $17.2 billion in dividends last year, making it the second-largest dividend payer in the S&P 500. Exxon has also increased its dividend for an industry-leading 43 straight years. As a result, Exxon has delivered peer-leading total shareholder returns since 2019. While Exxon leads in most categories, that's not to say Chevron is an also-ran. It has delivered the highest dividend growth rate in its peer group over the past decade. Chevron also has the lowest breakeven level in its peer group (less than $50 a barrel to fund its capital program and dividend), the best cash margins, the lowest reinvestment rate, and the highest new project returns. Exxon and Chevron are both operating under five-year plans. Exxon raised its 2030 plan last December. The oil giant now expects to deliver $25 billion in earnings growth and $35 billion in cash flow growth by 2030 at the same prices and margins as 2024. That implies 13% annual earnings-per-share growth and double-digit cash flow growth, both of which will be even higher on a per-share basis due to its share repurchase program. Exxon also expects to deliver $145 billion in cumulative free cash flow through 2030 at $65 oil, supporting continued dividend growth (current yield over 2.5%) and share repurchases. The company expects a combination of high-return capital projects and an additional $5 billion in structural cost savings to support its plan. Chevron has a similar strategy of investing in high-return capital projects and delivering structural cost savings. This approach positions it to deliver more than 10% annual adjusted earnings per share and free cash flow growth through 2030. That should give Chevron the fuel to continue increasing its dividend (current yield of more than 3.5%) while repurchasing $10 billion to $20 billion of shares each year. That's enough to retire about 3% to 6% of its outstanding shares annually. Meanwhile, both companies expect to continue growing beyond 2030. In addition to investing in oil and gas, both are growing their lower-carbon energy platforms. Exxon expects its new businesses (Proxxima systems, carbon materials, carbon capture, hydrogen, lithium, and others) to potentially reach $13 billion in earnings by 2040, with a long growth runway beyond that. Meanwhile, Chevron is investing in biofuels, natural gas-fired power plants for AI, hydrogen, lithium, and carbon capture. These businesses have the potential to be meaningful future growth drivers. I think Chevron is a great oil stock to buy, especially if you're seeking dividend income. It offers a higher current yield and could continue to grow its payout faster than Exxon in the future. However, if you're seeking to buy the best oil stock in the world, that's ExxonMobil. It's the undisputed industry leader in earnings, returns, cost-savings, and balance sheet strength. Meanwhile, it has the fuel to deliver robust growth through 2030 and beyond, which could enable it to continue delivering leading total returns over the long term.
